name: CreditAccess Grameen Ltd
about: CreditAccess Grameen Limited is registered as a non-deposit accepting NBFC - Microfinance Institution with the RBI. It is engaged in providing microfinance services to women who are enrolled as members and organized as Joint Liability Groups. It also uses its distribution channel to provide certain other financial products and services to the members. [1]

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth, so conversion ratios are not meaningful.

flags.text: Gross NPA fell from 4.70% to 2.18% in a year: asset quality is improving

business.what: CreditAccess Grameen lends to customers, mainly women in Group Loans, plus Individual Business, secured business, affordable housing and 2-wheeler loans. It earns interest income on these loans, funded by borrowings from more than 80 lenders at a blended cost of about 9%.

segments.name: Group Loans
segments.share: ~77% of AUM (derived from INR 23,746 Cr of INR 30,946 Cr)
segments.comment: AUM fell about 2% since FY27 start on write-offs and graduation; growth expected to return.

segments.name: Retail Finance
segments.comment: AUM reached INR 7,200 Cr; secured book up 60.9% YoY to INR 695 Cr.

kpis.value: INR 6,355 Cr, up 19.4% YoY and 4.1% QoQ

ledger.promise: FY27 AUM growth of at least 20% (later set at 20-25%)
ledger.quote: we need to do at least a 20% growth every year to reach our medium -term goal.
ledger.actual: Reiterated at 20-25% in Q2 FY27. AUM is not in our data. Borrowings rose 6.3% in H1 (23,641 to 25,128); group loan book fell 2% since start of FY27.

ledger.promise: Microfinance (group loan) growth of 10-12% in FY27
ledger.quote: when we look at microfinance growth, early days, maybe 10% to 12%
ledger.actual: Behind. Q2 FY27 call: group loan book down 2% since start of FY27 (write-offs, graduation). Management expects return to guided growth in H2.

ledger.quote: maybe for next year, we should see the NIMs anywhere between maybe 14% to 14.5%, in that range for some time
ledger.actual: Cut to 12.8-13.2% in Q4 FY26, then raised to 14.4-14.7% in Q2 FY27. Reported NIM is not in our data.

ledger.quote: Our FY27 credit cost guidance of 4% to 4.5% reflects a new PAR 15 accretion rate of 30 -35 bps per month.
ledger.actual: Lowered to 3-4% in Q4 FY26. Q1 FY27 said lower end; Q2 FY27 said 3.5-4%, with Q3 to inch up. Reported credit cost not in data.

ledger.quote: we will try to maintain our ROAs in 4 .0-4.5% range.
ledger.actual: Raised to ROA 5.2-5.8%, ROE 21-24% in Q2 FY27. H1 FY27 PAT 995 (493+502) is 128% of FY26 PAT of 778. Assets not given.

ledger.quote: For FY27, we are guiding an AUM growth of 20.0-25.0%, NIM of 12.8-13.2%, cost to income of 33.0-35.0%, credit cost of 3.0-4.0%, ROA of 4.0-4.8%, and an ROE of 16.0-20.0%.
ledger.actual: Guidance improved to 29-30% in Q2 FY27. Ratio not in our data. Revenue up 26.3% YoY in Q2 FY27 (1,904 vs 1,508).

ledger.quote: we would want to do a cross-cycle ROA of 4% and ROE of around 16%-17% on a cross cycle.
ledger.actual: Raised to ROA 4.5%, ROE 18-20% (Q1 FY27), then steady-state ROA 4.5-5% (Q2 FY27). Needs a full cycle to check.

ledger.promise: Stage 1 provisioning to rise toward 1.5% in Q4 FY26
ledger.quote: we should see the Stage 1 provisioning inch up closer to 1.5%. So that should happen in fourth quarter.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 call: ECL provision rate 1.63%, after an extra 39 provision in Q4. Q1 FY27: Stage 1 PCR 1.63%, above the 1.5% guided.

ledger.promise: Borrowing cost to fall about 10 bps a quarter for 2-3 quarters
ledger.quote: borrowing cost incrementally, we do see dropping by 10 bps every quarter for at least next 2 to 3 quarters
ledger.actual: Q2 FY27 call: marginal cost of borrowing rose slightly in Q2, blamed on borrowing mix. Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 figures not reported in materials.

ledger.promise: Up to 50 bps lending rate cut by end of Q2 FY27
ledger.quote: by end of Q2 FY27, probably can look at a 50 bps price cut if we are able to hold the asset quality
ledger.actual: Q2 FY27 call moves first 50 bps cut to Q3 FY27, then Q4 and Q1 FY28. Later cuts happen only if credit cost holds at 3%.

ledger.promise: About 1 lakh new borrowers a month for rest of FY27
ledger.quote: adding close to an average of 1 Lakh borrowers per month going forward
ledger.actual: Q2 FY27: about 80,000 a month. More than 1 lakh restated as an 'ideal' target with no date.

ledger.promise: Return with clearer credit cost guidance by May 2026
ledger.quote: probably by May, we will try and come back with a clearer guidance.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 call (May 2026) gave full FY27 guidance, including credit cost of 3-4%.

current_guidance.quote: We raised our profitability guidance for FY27, ROA of 5.2% to 5.8% versus 4% to 4.8% earlier
and ROE of 21% to 24% versus 16% to 20% earlier
We expect a NIM of 14.4% to 14.7% as against 12.8% to 13.2% guided earlier
Cost to income may range between 29% to 30% as operating costs remain well under control
We retain our AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25%, supported by return to growth in Group Loan portfolio

current_guidance.target: 3-4% formally; 3.5-4% steer (Q1 FY27 had pointed to the lower end)
current_guidance.quote: you should assume that it will be somewhere between 3.5% to 4%

current_guidance.target: 50 bps each in Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28; later cuts only if credit cost holds at 3%
current_guidance.quote: we will pass on 50 bps in third quarter, fourth quarter and next year's Q1

current_guidance.target: 10-12%; group loan growth back to guided levels in H2
current_guidance.quote: Microfinance, as we said in our strategic plan, could be range bound in the range of anywhere between 10% to 12%.

current_guidance.target: More than 1 lakh (now about 80,000), no date
current_guidance.quote: Ideally, we would like to publish more than 1 Lakh customers every month, and that's the target that we are working on.
We remain fully committed to our medium -term guidance of INR 50,000 Crore AUM by calendar year 2028

credibility.label: mixed
credibility.summary: FY26 credit cost came in worse than the 5.5-6.0% guidance and ROA/ROE missed the low end of guidance (management said this on the Q4 FY26 call), but FY27 profit is running well ahead: H1 PAT of 995 already exceeds FY26's 778 and drove the Q2 upgrade. Smaller operating promises have slipped (borrowing cost, timing of rate cuts, customer additions, group loan growth), and NIM guidance has moved 14-14.5% to 12.8-13.2% to 14.4-14.7% in nine months, so point guidance has been an unreliable anchor.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Profitability has recovered enough to raise FY27 ROA to 5.2-5.8% and ROE to 21-24%.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: PAT rose from 126 (Q2 FY26) to 502 (Q2 FY27). H1 FY27 PAT of 995 exceeds FY26 full-year 778. TTM PAT 1,587.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: AUM growth of 20-25% retained for FY27, helped by group loans returning to growth.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Borrowings grew only 6.3% from FY26-end (23,641 to 25,128) and the group loan book fell 2% in H1, so H2 needs a sharp pickup. Revenue up 26.3% YoY in Q2 may reflect lower credit stress more than loan growth; the materials cannot separate the two.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Credit cost easing allows rate cuts while protecting profit; Q1 FY27 pointed to the lower end of 3-4%.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: By Q2 the steer moved to 3.5-4%, with Q3 to inch up (flood-related PAR in Aug-Sep, Maharashtra drought). Profit growth flattened: PAT 493 to 502 QoQ, EBITDA margin 37.9% to 36.1%.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Incremental borrowing cost to fall about 10 bps a quarter for 2-3 quarters.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q2 FY27 call says marginal borrowing cost rose slightly in Q2 because of the borrowing mix.

bull.point: Earnings run-rate already supports a much higher FY27 profit than FY26
bull.evidence: Q1 and Q2 FY27 PAT of 493 and 502 give H1 995 against FY26 PAT of 778; TTM PAT 1,587.

bull.point: Provision buffer built ahead of time
bull.evidence: Stage 1 provisioning raised to 1.63%, above the 1.5% guided, including an extra 39 in Q4 FY26 for a major external event scenario.
bull.source: Q4 FY26 call p4; Q1 FY27 call p11

bull.point: Management says it has pricing room to absorb higher credit cost
bull.evidence: Says it can pass through credit cost up to 4.5-5% and still protect ROA of about 4.5-5%, and that rate cuts depend on credit cost holding at 3%.

bear.point: Loan growth is behind the 20-25% AUM guide
bear.evidence: Group loan book down 2% in H1 FY27; borrowings up only 6.3% from FY26-end; customer additions about 80,000 a month against a 1 lakh target.
bear.source: Q2 FY27 call p4, p16; reported numbers

bear.point: Credit cost is moving up again
bear.evidence: Steer moved from the lower end of 3-4% (Q1) to 3.5-4% (Q2), with Q3 expected higher; flood-related PAR increase and requests from Maharashtra drought-hit borrowers for more time to repay. FY26 credit cost came in worse than guidance.
bear.source: Q1 FY27 call p11; Q2 FY27 call p4, p5, p7, p11; Q4 FY26 call p4

bear.point: Margin pressure from planned rate cuts
bear.evidence: 150 bps of lending rate cuts planned over Q3 FY27 to Q1 FY28, while marginal borrowing cost rose in Q2; assets take 15-18 months to reprice, so NIM pressure would carry into FY28.
bear.source: Q2 FY27 call p6, p7; Q1 FY27 call p10
